name: Scapular Pull-Up on Rings
description: The ring scapular pull-up is performed identically to the bar version — shoulder blades depressed and retracted without elbow flexion — but the unstable ring surface adds a rotational challenge that increases demand on the serratus anterior and rotator cuff stabilizers. It is a superior proprioceptive warm-up and shoulder health drill for ring athletes.

execution.starting_position: Hang from gymnastic rings at shoulder width with arms fully extended. Rings should be turned out slightly.
execution.setup_instructions: Set ring height to allow full dead-hang with feet off the ground. Use a grip with palms facing each other (neutral grip).
steps: Step 1: Begin in a dead hang, body relaxed.
Step 2: Without bending elbows, depress and retract the scapulae, elevating the body slightly.
Step 3: Hold the depressed position 1-2 seconds.
Step 4: Return slowly to the resting dead-hang.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as scapulae depress. Inhale returning to dead hang.
common_mistakes: Bending elbows — this defeats the purpose of the drill
Allowing the rings to swing excessively — maintain control
safety_considerations: Inspect ring straps and anchor points before hanging
Build wrist and grip tolerance before full dead hangs
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Shoulder blades travel from resting elevated position to maximally depressed.
coaching_cues: Shoulder blades into your back pockets
Control the rings — do not let them spin
